Consider the following PR description:
Array indexing syntax not properly parsed

#### Description

When parsing SQL with array indexing syntax like `col[1]` or `somefunc()[1]`, the parser fails to properly group the identifier with its array indices. This causes issues when trying to access array indices from parsed identifiers.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import sqlparse

# Simple array index
p = sqlparse.parse('col[1]')[0].tokens
print(f"Number of tokens: {len(p)}")
print(f"Expected: 1, Got: {len(p)}")

# Try to get array indices
try:
    indices = list(p[0].get_array_indices())
    print(f"Array indices found: {len(indices)}")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error getting array indices: {e}")

# Function result with array index
p2 = sqlparse.parse('somefunc()[1]')[0].tokens
print(f"Function array tokens: {len(p2)}")

# 2D array indexing
p3 = sqlparse.parse('col[x][(y+1)*2]')[0].tokens
print(f"2D array tokens: {len(p3)}")

# Schema qualified array
p4 = sqlparse.parse('schem.col[1]')[0].tokens
print(f"Schema qualified array tokens: {len(p4)}")
```

The parser should group array indexing syntax into single identifiers, but currently fails to do so properly.
